task: SCS-002 Commerce MVP — Stage 3 business logic (Issue #55, ADR-0013): the full commerce contour on the Stage 2 skeleton — catalog (Product → Offer → Price), mutable Cart, checkout as a business command, immutable Order purchase facts with the mutable payment state — behind the same enforcement chain, IS-005 guard, audit journal and published client. Live operations: twelve — create and read one owned Product, define one Offer, set one Price, open/read/mutate one owned Cart, checkout, read one owned Order, record its payment.

invariants: C-001 every product, offer, price, cart, cart line, order and order line has exactly one data owner
C-002 a subject of Tenant A never reaches Commerce data of Tenant B, including by changing an identifier or a caller-supplied tenant_id
C-003 a request with an IS-003 DENY never reaches the owned-data operation
C-004 an authorization dependency failure or a malformed/non-authoritative dependency answer fails closed to DENY
C-005 the effective tenant comes from IS-001; this component creates no second tenant-context mechanism
C-006 the public surface provides no access path that bypasses the Commerce enforcement boundary
C-007 security-sensitive refusals are auditable and observable with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where applicable
C-008 the internals of this component are not a consumer contract: a consumer receives the published client and values only
C-009 the catalog boundary is Product → Offer → Price: no Product.price exists, a price belongs to a sellable proposition, and no price books, tiers or pricing engines exist
C-010 every offer belongs to exactly one product of the same Tenant and every price to exactly one offer of the same Tenant: no orphan and no cross-tenant catalog record exists

C-011 the purchase facts of an Order (buyer, tenant, bought positions, captured prices) are immutable after creation; an OrderLine price snapshot is a copied value and is never recomputed from the current catalog

C-012 the payment state is the mutable Commerce-owned state/result bound to an Order; a payment-state change never touches the immutable purchase facts; no Payment Service, no payment provider and no gateway imitation exists
C-013 a buyer is an opaque buyer_identity_id: no customer, user or profile service exists and no identity internals are copied

C-014 Commerce reaches Learning — and Learning reaches Commerce — only through published contracts: no database, table or internal-module access in either direction, and no automatic paid-order → learning-access exists

product_model.note: A Product is what can be offered for sale in one Tenant (ADR-0013). tenant_id and owner_component are store facts of the record and are not published in the view. created_by is the opaque reference to the verified identity that created the product — Identity owns the profile, Commerce stores and never interprets the reference. The model is domain-agnostic: no Learning entities, no foreign keys into another schema, and no price — the price of a sellable proposition lives on the Price record, never here.

operations.purpose: create one owned Product in the effective tenant of the verified identity; a new Product is created ACTIVE
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The command has no pre-existing target: the IS-005 resource binding is empty, and the tenant binding is the effective tenant of the chain.

operations.purpose: serve one owned Product after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: define one sellable proposition of an existing Product of the effective tenant; a new Offer is created ACTIVE
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The command has no pre-existing target: the IS-005 resource binding is empty, and the tenant binding is the effective tenant of the chain.

operations.purpose: append one price to the price history of an existing Offer of the effective tenant; the new record never rewrites a past one
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The command has no pre-existing target: the IS-005 resource binding is empty, and the tenant binding is the effective tenant of the chain.

operations.purpose: open one cart for the verified subject in the effective tenant; the command carries no body and a new cart holds no lines
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The command has no pre-existing target: the IS-005 resource binding is empty, and the tenant binding is the effective tenant of the chain.

operations.purpose: serve one owned cart of the verified subject after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: add one offer of the cart's Tenant to the subject's own cart; a repeated offer increments its line
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded cart without a second effect, and a changed binding (cart, offer, quantity, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The IS-005 resource binding is the cart.

operations.purpose: set the quantity of one existing cart line of the subject's own cart to an absolute positive value
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded cart without a second effect, and a changed binding (cart, offer, quantity, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The IS-005 resource binding is the cart.

operations.purpose: remove one existing line from the subject's own cart
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded cart without a second effect, and a changed binding (cart, offer, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The IS-005 resource binding is the cart.

operations.purpose: convert one owned cart of the verified subject into an order: validate the selected offers and their current prices, create the Order with immutable purchase facts, consume the cart lines, and set PENDING_PAYMENT
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded order without a second order, and a changed binding (cart, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The IS-005 resource binding is the cart. Concurrent checkouts of the same cart are serialized in the cart's domain critical section: the second one refuses with cart_empty.

operations.purpose: serve one owned order of the verified subject after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: record one PENDING_PAYMENT order of the verified subject as paid; the only payment-state move that exists
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded order without a second move, and a changed binding (order, identity, tenant, operation) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The IS-005 resource binding is the order. Concurrent payments of the same order are serialized in the order's domain critical section: only the first PENDING_PAYMENT → PAID move succeeds.

enforcement_model.passed_through_denials: the published deny reasons of IS-003, unchanged
enforcement_model.nonauthoritative_answers: an answer outside the published decision model of IS-003 — including an ALLOW with a reason other than permitted and a DENY with an unknown reason — fails closed as authorization_unavailable

product_catalog.boundary: Product → Offer → Price: an Offer links exactly one Product to a sellable proposition within the same Tenant, and a Price is a first-class price concept attached to the sellable proposition; collapsing the boundary to Product.price is not allowed
product_catalog.product: a new Product is created ACTIVE in the effective tenant of the verified identity; catalog lifecycle transitions arrive in a later slice
product_catalog.offer_and_price: define-offer and set-price are live commands: an Offer is defined under an existing Product of the effective tenant, a Price is appended to the price history of an existing Offer of the effective tenant; parentage stays same-tenant and history stays append-only
product_catalog.cart_and_order: open/read/mutate cart, checkout, read order and record payment are live commands: a subject reaches only its own carts and orders; checkout converts the selected offers at their current prices into immutable purchase facts, consumes the cart lines and sets PENDING_PAYMENT; only the PENDING_PAYMENT → PAID move exists
product_catalog.no_checkout_entity: Checkout is a business command, not an entity: no persistent Checkout record exists and none is planned without a proven need and a separate decision
product_catalog.no_payment_service: payment is the mutable commercial state/result bound to an Order and owned by Commerce; no Payment Service, no provider integration and no gateway imitation exist

refusal_semantics.principle: a refusal is data with a stable machine-readable code and reason, audited with request_id and correlation_id; nothing about this surface can be mistaken for a served record

error.message: the stable message of the code

shape.request_id: the request_id the refusal was audited with
shape.correlation_id: the correlation_id the refusal was audited with

AUTHORIZATION_DENIED.reasons: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch, buyer_mismatch

NOT_FOUND.reasons: product_unknown, offer_unknown, price_unknown, cart_unknown, order_unknown, cart_line_unknown

INVALID_REQUEST.message: Request does not match the published contract.
INVALID_REQUEST.note: defence in depth: the schema handler refuses a request the published contract cannot read (e.g. a command body with a missing field, a wrong type or a declared-unknown field) before any handler runs; the stable reason is malformed_request

INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.message: Operation is not valid for the current state.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.message: An Idempotency-Key header is required for this operation.

IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.message: The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.

envelope.note: The HTTP status selects the code; the stable internal reason is preserved in error.details.reason; request_id and correlation_id match the audit record of the refusal.

refused.403: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch, buyer_mismatch
refused.404: product_unknown, offer_unknown, price_unknown, cart_unknown, order_unknown, cart_line_unknown

refusal_semantics.served: HTTP 200/201 with the published representation — product, offer, price, cart or order — produced only by the owned-data operation at the end of the enforcement chain

consumer_surface.transport: commerce_service.transport.open_channel + commerce_service.transport.call_contract — the published HTTP contract executed in process over an opaque channel handle (ARCHITECTURE.md §1.1 interaction mode API, Level 0)
errors: commerce_service.errors.AccessRefused — the access did not happen; the reason is one of the published refusal reasons (400/401/403/404/409/422/503), carried in error.details.reason, with the request_id/correlation_id of the refusal
commerce_service.errors.ContractViolation — the contract transport failed or answered outside its published shape (including any non-envelope shape); a consumer must fail closed
guarantees: values only: no commerce store, audit journal, engine reference or deployment is reachable through the published surface
the published client holds no callable and no credential: its state is one channel handle, so walking the client and its class reaches neither the component's ASGI application nor its internals
the subject credential is supplied per access and verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision: a consumer cannot assert who the subject is
the ASGI application is never handed out: it stays behind the provider-side channel table, and a channel is revoked when the consumer drops the client
importing the published module binds no reference to commerce_service.transport — its namespace holds no module object, no channel table and no transport type
an unknown or revoked channel handle raises ContractViolation, so there is no permissive fallback and a handle cannot be guessed
every access runs through the same routing, enforcement chain and audit code that serves an HTTP request
there is no product listing, bulk export, search, pagination or raw-store operation: the twelve published operations are the only access paths, and all are enforced
the state-changing commands own no second idempotency mechanism: each is delivered to the IS-005 guard, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict
composition_root_only: the contract application itself (the ASGI application) — a consumer component must not own or re-export it
the contract channel table commerce_service.transport._CHANNELS — a handle-to-application mapping owned by the component
consumer_surface.note: The deployment object is composition-internal: it assembles engine, store and contract application for the composition root and for this component's own tests and is never handed to a consumer. This component composes no other component and publishes no module-level demo application: a demo of a data owner needs a composed Platform Instance with a live decision dependency, and composing one is the job of a composition root.

consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of authorization, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: deployment secret resolved by the composition root: the service identity of this component
consumes.note: The access decision is read per access and never cached. The resource's owning Tenant stated in the question comes from this component's own store — or, for the create commands whose targets do not exist yet, from the effective tenant of the verified identity — never from a caller claim (LAW-16a).
consumes.dependency_isolation: No module of commerce imports authorization_service, identity_service or tenant_authority: the published client is adapted at the composition boundary and only values owned by this component reach the enforcement logic (ARCHITECTURE.md 1.1, 6.1, LAW-04).

consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of identity, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: the subject credential presented on the published surface; the adapter adds nothing
consumes.note: Consumed by exactly the four create commands — product, offer, price, cart — whose targets do not exist yet, so the resource Tenant of their authorization questions can only be the effective tenant of the verified identity (the chain Identity -> effective tenant -> Authorization -> Commerce ownership boundary). The adapter is structural over the published client, like its sibling for IS-003; the composition root wires it, and no module of commerce imports identity_service. No second identity or tenant mechanism exists: the port carries the answer of IS-001 and nothing else.

events.note: SCS-002 Stage 3 publishes no inter-component events and does not simulate a broker. The access audit journal is owned data, not a public event contract.

data_export_cdc.note: No CDC or bulk export stream is implemented in this slice. A bulk path would be a bypass risk for the enforcement boundary and is deliberately out of this slice.

ui.note: Class A Business System / SCS; UI is out of this Level 0 slice. Every published operation is proven at the API boundary.

platform_id.description: Identifier of the Platform Instance this data owner serves.

datasets.name: products
datasets.note: Every product has exactly one data owner and belongs to exactly one Tenant; lifecycle is exactly ACTIVE; the Tenant comes from the verified identity through the published chain, never from a caller claim. Domain-agnostic: no Learning internals and no price — the price of a sellable proposition lives on the Price record.

datasets.name: offers
datasets.note: Every offer links exactly one Product to a sellable proposition within the same Tenant; created only under an existing Product of that Tenant. Lifecycle is exactly ACTIVE.

datasets.name: prices
datasets.note: Every price belongs to exactly one Offer of the same Tenant; amount is in minor currency units with an ISO currency code. Prices are append-only history: a new registration never rewrites a past record.

datasets.name: carts
datasets.note: Mutable pre-order state of one buyer (opaque buyer_identity_id) within one Tenant; not a commercial fact — it may change, be emptied or be abandoned without commercial consequence.

datasets.name: cart_lines
datasets.note: One selected Offer with a positive quantity per (Cart, Offer); the Cart and the Offer belong to the same Tenant as the line.

datasets.name: orders
datasets.note: The central commercial fact: what a specific buyer bought in a specific tenant. The purchase facts (buyer, tenant, bought positions) are immutable after creation; the payment state bound to the Order is the mutable lifecycle/result and changes only through the payment-state operation.

datasets.name: order_lines
datasets.note: One bought position per line with an immutable price snapshot at order time (copied amount/currency/quantity plus the Product/Offer references); never recomputed from the current catalog; no update operation exists.

datasets.name: payment_state
datasets.note: The mutable commercial state/result of payment of an Order (PENDING_PAYMENT → PAID), owned by Commerce. Stored as fields of the Order in this slice (ADR-0013 permits either storage form); a payment-state change never touches the immutable purchase facts. No Payment Service, no provider integration and no gateway imitation exist.

datasets.name: access_audit
datasets.note: Append-only journal of every access attempt — served or refused — with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where known.

notes: This component owns no identity, no permission grant, no tenant registry and no tenant state: those belong to identity, authorization and tenant_authority and are read through their published contracts.
The Product → Offer → Price parentage is registered, never declared by a caller: the store refuses orphan and cross-tenant children, duplicate identifiers and invalid content at registration.
Checkout is a business command, not an entity: no persistent Checkout record exists in any dataset.

audit.journal: internal append-only journal owned by commerce
audit.refusal_audit_scope: every refusal of the published contract, including a request rejected by the contract schema before any handler runs and a refusal produced because the decision dependency did not answer; the record carries request_id and correlation_id of the caller
audit.note: Audit is owned data, not a public event contract, and is not readable through the published surface.

observability.saga_id: absent — this component runs no inter-component sagas

authn.note: The subject credential presented on the public surface is verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision; this component verifies no credential itself. When asking IS-003, this component authenticates with its own service identity (demo: authz-svc-token-commerce).

authz.note: ALLOW from IS-003 is not direct data access: the data owner remains the final enforcement boundary (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2). A decision that cannot be obtained is a denial. The ten operations of this slice each carry their own grant — no role or policy logic exists inside Commerce. The four create commands have no pre-existing target, so their authorization questions name the effective tenant of the verified identity resolved through IS-001; no second identity, tenant, authorization or idempotency mechanism is introduced.

compatibility_policy.reason_codes: adding a refusal reason is a minor change; removing or redefining one is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.enforcement_chain: reordering or removing a step is a breaking change: the order is part of the published behaviour
compatibility_policy.product_model: adding a field to the product representation is a minor change; changing the eight published fields is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.error_envelope: the approved envelope shape is part of the contract; changing error/code/message/details/request_id/correlation_id is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.catalog_growth: Stage 3 grew the surface additively (0.1.0 → 0.2.0): new Offer, Price, Cart, Checkout, Order and payment-state operations, schemas, reasons and grants without changing any existing operation, reason or representation — the policy this entry states for further growth. The product lifecycle is exactly ACTIVE; adding product lifecycle states or transitions is a new architectural decision, not a silent change.

dependencies.direction: commerce -> idempotency (exactly-once delivery of the state-changing commands)
dependencies.note: SCS-002 implements no second idempotency mechanism: every state-changing command identity (operation, payload fingerprint) is delivered to IS-005, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict.

dependencies.direction: commerce -> identity (tenant context of the verified subject for the create commands without a target)
dependencies.note: Consumed only because the four create commands have no pre-existing resource whose Tenant the store could state. The effective tenant still comes from IS-001 and from nowhere else; a caller-supplied tenant_id remains a cross-check (LAW-16a).
